01 The commons

Paint knowledge belongs at the table.

Paint ranges grow. Names change. Useful details get scattered across bottles, websites, and hobby tables. Paint Commons brings those details into one shared reference that the community can keep improving.

The goal is simple: a living catalog of miniature paints, with clear sources and a history of corrections. Something painters can consult, contributors can improve, and developers can build on.

Know what it is.

Connect manufacturers, paint ranges, product codes, and barcodes through stable paint records.

Understand the evidence.

Keep swatch observations and suggested equivalents tied to their sources and conditions.

Keep it useful.

Preserve attribution and correction history as new paints arrive and old information changes.

03 Take part

You don’t need to know every paint.
Just help with one.

Fill a gap.

Help identify a missing paint, a new range, or a product code that hasn’t been recorded.

Make a correction.

Spot a renamed paint, a duplicate, or an incorrect finish? A precise correction makes the next visit better.

Bring the evidence.

Share a source or a swatch with its conditions. Give credit, and be clear about what’s observed and what’s inferred.

How is Paint Commons different from Stipplewise?

Paint Commons is the shared, openly accessible paint reference. Stipplewise is a separate painting companion app for personal collections and painting workflows. The planned connection lets Stipplewise contribute to and use the shared catalog, alongside other tools.

Will my personal collection become public?

Personal inventory, wishlists, projects, drafts, and unsubmitted photos stay separate from the Commons. The planned contribution process publishes only information you explicitly submit and maintainers approve.

Can a swatch tell me how a paint will look?

A swatch is an observation, not a promise. Lighting, camera settings, surface, and application all matter. Metallic and colour-shift paints need more context than a single digital value. Suggested equivalents should include evidence and uncertainty.

What does “open” mean for the project?

The goal is portable records, transparent corrections, attribution, and versioned public releases. Data licensing, source redistribution rights, and contributor guidelines are still being worked through; a final license has not yet been selected.

A better reference, one contribution at a time.

For the painter at the next table. And the next generation of tools.
